name: UT Phänomen
classification_notes: Features horizontal contrast — thicker horizontals than verticals — directly inverting the conventional stress axis of traditional type. Influenced by MICR E-13B banking typography, placing it in the tradition of reverse-contrast and industrial display lettering with a postdigital theoretical framing.
summary: A display face with horizontal contrast drawn from MICR E-13B banking typography and postdigital aesthetics.
description: UT Phänomen inverts the conventional stress axis: horizontals are heavy where verticals are light, taking direct cues from MICR E-13B, the magnetic ink character recognition font used on bank cheques. The result is an industrial, technically-inflected display typeface that sits within the reverse-contrast lettering tradition. It suits editorial and brand contexts where a postdigital, machine-influenced aesthetic is the point.
foundry_blurb: A typeface with horizontal contrast that continues Undt's exploration into postdigital aesthetics, influenced in part by MICR E-13B, the magnetic ink character recognition font developed by the Stanford Research Institute and General Electric Computer Laboratory. Designer Marcus Leis Allion describes UNDT as working at a question of form, moving between the history of writing and the aesthetics of technical mediation.
